what_its_for: Dihydroergotamine is used to treat migraine headaches, sometimes with or without an aura (visual disturbances like flashing lights). It works by tightening blood vessels in your brain to relieve migraine pain. It is NOT used to prevent migraines — only to treat them once they start.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a nasal spray or as an injection. For the NASAL SPRAY: Blow your nose gently first. Prime the pump before your first use by pumping it 4 times into the air. Tilt your head slightly forward, insert the tip into one nostril, and spray while breathing in gently through your nose. Repeat in the other nostril. Do NOT sniff deeply or blow your nose for 15 minutes after using it. For the INJECTION (D.H.E. 45): This is given under the skin or into a muscle. Your doctor or nurse will show you exactly how to give the injection. Always follow their instructions carefully. Use this medicine as soon as your migraine starts for the best results.
dosing: NASAL SPRAY (Migranal/Trudhesa): The usual dose is one spray (0.5 mg) into each nostril. You may repeat this after 15 minutes if needed. Do NOT use more than 3 mg (6 sprays) in one migraine attack, and no more than 4 mg (8 sprays) in any 7-day period. INJECTION: The usual dose is 1 mg injected under the skin or into a muscle. This can be repeated every hour if needed, up to 3 mg total in one day and no more than 6 mg in one week. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions, as doses can vary.
missed_dose: Dihydroergotamine is used only when you have a migraine — it is NOT taken on a regular daily schedule. If you have a migraine and forget to take it early on, you can still try taking it, but it works best when taken as soon as your migraine begins. Do NOT double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the nasal spray away from light and heat. Do NOT freeze it. Keep the nasal spray upright when storing. Once a nasal spray bottle is opened, use it within 8 hours and then throw it away — do not save leftover medication in an open bottle. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: AVOID other migraine medicines called triptans (such as sumatriptan, rizatriptan) within 24 hours of using this medicine. AVOID ergot-type medicines (like ergotamine) at the same time. AVOID strong antifungal medicines (like ketoconazole, itraconazole), certain antibiotics (like erythromycin, clarithromycin), and HIV medications — these can cause dangerous interactions. AVOID smoking, as it can increase the risk of serious side effects on your blood vessels. AVOID using this medicine more than 10 days per month — overuse can actually cause more frequent headaches (called medication overuse headache). AVOID breastfeeding while using this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; pain, numbness, or color changes (blue or pale) in your fingers or toes; sudden severe headache that is different from your usual migraines; shortness of breath; rapid or irregular heartbeat; signs of poor blood flow such as cold or numb hands and feet; stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting that is severe; muscle pain or weakness; vision changes; or any signs of stroke such as sudden weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or confusion. Also call your doctor if your migraines are not getting better or are getting worse.
when_it_works: Dihydroergotamine usually starts to relieve migraine pain within 30 minutes to 2 hours after using the nasal spray. The injection may work a little faster. It works best when you use it as soon as your migraine starts. It may not work as well if you wait until the headache is very severe.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Do NOT use this medicine if you are pregnant. It can cause harm to an unborn baby, including reduced blood flow. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Do NOT use this medicine while breastfeeding, as it passes into breast milk and can harm the baby. ELDERLY (over 65): Use with extra caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects on blood vessels and may have a higher risk of side effects. CHILDREN: Safety in children under 6 years old has not been well established. Use in children should only be under close medical supervision. HEART OR BLOOD VESSEL DISEASE: Do NOT use this medicine if you have coronary artery disease, a history of heart attack or stroke, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or poor circulation in your legs or arms. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Use with caution if you have kidney or liver disease — your doctor may need to adjust your dose or choose a different treatment.
